purpose: Prototype v6r: how much does the per-person verdict (does the row's change exceed the person's own distance between two parts: 1, 1/2 or 0, count 1 of v6b.one) depend on which fixed two-part split builds it, odd/even sentences or halves? Asked by the pre-review of outline v14 for the Journal of Writing Research (round 8, R3 m1): the part-to-part reliability of the components is not the reliability of the verdict that a reader would report per person (Parsons et al. 2019: 'Reliability should be estimated for the actual outcome measures to be analysed'). Decided by the researcher (decision 37 of .steering/20261108-paper-a-jowr-reframe). Per dataset, row and stage, on the persons who are rule persons under both splits (the common persons), the two splits' verdicts are cross-tabulated: the share of common persons whose two verdicts agree, the table of disagreements by direction, the agreement expected by chance from the two splits' shares on the same persons, and Cohen's kappa beside. All descriptions.
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-11-09 after seeing the records and notes of v6k-v6q and the pre-review of outline v14 (round 8). The persons are v6m's (= v6n's to v6q's), whose values have been seen, including every stage's share per split on its rule persons (v6n, v6q). No cross-tabulation of the two splits' verdicts per person, and no share over the common persons, has been computed or looked at; the sizes of the common sets have not been computed. A first draft was sent to Codex (codex-consult, the conditions text and earlier aggregate results only, no data; .steering/20261109-v6r-split-agreement/codex-consult-output.md) and changed after its points (decision 1 of that folder).
status: Description (status d) throughout: v6m's persons with v6m's to v6q's values seen. The readings below are fixed before any new value is seen; they are not a confirmation. No rule and no label: v6k's rule and labels are not re-evaluated.

sources.v6n: works/conditions/prototype_v6n.json and results/prototype_v6n/record.json: the persons, rows, rule cells (rule_persons) per split with R_loc and R_mean on the same persons, count 1 cells, and their keys; v6n's code is imported.
sources.v6p: works/conditions/prototype_v6p.json and results/prototype_v6p/record.json: the ledger of the sets already written per split and row (count 1 cells, rule cells, v6o's families, v6p's written families) and v6p's small_sets.
sources.v6q: works/conditions/prototype_v6q.json and results/prototype_v6q/record.json: I[2] (I's word-start mean alone) on I's rule persons, and I[2]'s own ledger per split and row.

participants.persons: v6n's (v6m's draw, reused; v6n's checks of the id lists run).
participants.rule_persons: per dataset, split, row and stage, v6n's rule persons of the stage (the persons with the stage and R in the text and the row). For R_loc and R_mean: I's rule persons (as read through the gate in v6q). For I[2]: I's rule persons (v6q).
participants.common_persons: per dataset, row and stage, the persons who are rule persons of the stage under both splits (intersection of the two rule sets; the persons are indexed alike in both splits). Written: the number of common persons, the two rule sets' numbers, and the numbers who are rule persons under one split only (odd/even only, halves only). I[2]'s common set is checked equal to I's (both are I's rule persons).

units_parts: as v6n: sentences (counting 'before'); split odd/even (sentences alternately to the two parts) and halves (the first and second half of the sentences). The halves split also separates earlier from later stages of writing, so a disagreement mixes the noise of splitting with this difference in what the two splits compare (limits).

stages.main: v6k's rule stages U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000 and I, v6q's I[2], and the references R_loc and R_mean. U_med, B_complete@2000 and Bsd_complete@2000 are not counted.
stages.verdict: per person, split, row and stage: the contribution of count 1 (v6b.one; v6o's contrib_base_change). With x_h the stage's vector of part h (h = 0, 1) in the text and y_h in the row, each component j divided by s_j, the standard deviation of component j over all persons and both parts of the text in that split's rule cell (components with s_j = 0 are dropped, as in contrib_base_change): base = || x_0/s - x_1/s ||, change = ( || y_0/s - x_0/s || + || y_1/s - x_1/s || ) / 2 (Euclidean norms); contribution 1 if change > base, 1/2 if change == base in floating point (as computed by contrib_base_change, whose order of operations is v6m's own_contrib and checked equal), 0 if less. The scale is that of the cell v6n reported, so the two splits' scales differ, and each person's verdict per split is exactly the one inside v6n's share. For I[2] (one number) the scale cancels (v6q).
stages.fixed: a stage fixed by construction under a row in either split (U@2000 and B@2000 under the inside rows; B@2000 under shuffled_in_halves/before with halves: v6p's fixed) is not counted under either split, whatever its contributions (change is 0, so they are 0 or 1/2); it is listed as fixed.

rows: v6n's inside_75, inside_100 and cross_100, and v6k's shuffled/before and shuffled_in_halves/before (v6k's main rows; inside/before is inside_100 and is left out). The other dose rows are not counted. shuffled_in_halves shuffles within the halves of the text, so it is not the same operation relative to the two splits; it is listed and not read as a split-only comparison.

cells.agreement: per dataset, row and stage on the common persons: the full 3 x 3 table of the two splits' contributions (odd/even by halves, categories 0, 1/2 and 1; counts over the common persons); the agreement p_o = share on the diagonal, with the 95% percentile interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples of the common persons (v6.ci); the disagreements '1->0' (1 under odd/even, 0 under halves) and '0->1', and the four involving 1/2 kept apart; each split's share (mean contribution) and its three category proportions on the common persons; the chance agreement p_e = sum over the three categories of the product of the two splits' category proportions on the common persons (the agreement expected if the two verdicts were paired independently with these marginal distributions); Cohen's kappa = (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e) when p_e < 1, else not written (reason 'p_e = 1'); kappa's interval over the same resamples with p_e recomputed in each, written only if p_e < 1 in every resample (else the number of resamples with p_e = 1 is written and no interval); and, beside and not recomputed, each split's class of the stage on its own rule persons and the cell's gate state per split (v6n).
cells.keys: numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 101, dataset, task, stage, row index, 7, 9, 0]) with v6n's dataset, task and row indices, the stage indices of v6k-v6n (U 2, B 3, Bsd 4, I 5, R_loc 8, R_mean 12) and v6q's 22 for I[2]; 7 marks the pair of splits (v6b's baselines are 0 and 1) and 9 a whole cell, so no key is shared with v6k-v6q.

written_plan.rule: the common set is a new set. Per dataset, split, row and stage, before anything is written: the ledger of that split's quantity is rebuilt as v6p's (the pooled ledger of the row: count 1 cells, rule cells, v6o's families, v6p's written families; and the stage's own ledger) and, for I[2], v6q's own ledger; the common set is added only if no set of 1-4 persons becomes linearly derivable that was not derivable before (v6p's small_sets, both the pooled and the stage's ledger). A cell is written only if its common set is admitted under both splits; otherwise only the numbers of persons are written (reason 'derivable'). An admitted common set stays in the ledgers for the later stages of the row (order U, B, Bsd, I, I[2], R_loc, R_mean). The agreement indicator is a new per-person quantity written over one set per row and stage; a common set of fewer than 5 persons is not written. The disagreement counts and the shares on the common persons are over the common persons and add no set. 'Fewer than 5' counts persons. A withheld cell's numbers of persons are written, as in v6p and v6q (the numbers of the two rule sets are already written by v6n).
written_plan.guarantee: linear only, as in v6p and v6q: it does not cover inference from the values' constraints (contributions take three values, so counts of 0 in the table tell something of every member); counts over 5 or more persons are written as in v6k-v6q.
written_plan.table: the counts of the 3 x 3 table and of the disagreements are counts over the common persons (5 or more), not summaries over the persons of a cell of the table, and are written however small (as v6q's count of persons with I[2] below I); a table cell is not suppressed. Identity checked: the difference of the two shares times the common persons equals ('1->0' - '0->1') + 1/2 x (('1->1/2' + '1/2->0') - ('1/2->1' + '0->1/2')).

primary: named before running and read in this order. (1) Read first, chosen because of known results (the rows where the gate R_loc reaches in at least one split, v6n): 1 - p_o, p_o's interval, p_e and kappa of I, I[2] and R_loc at LWP inside_75 and inside_100, with the table. (2) The primary cells: every counted stage at inside_75, inside_100 and cross_100 in both datasets (1 - p_o, interval, p_e, kappa, the two shares on the common persons, the table). (3) The shuffles: listed as a table and not read one by one. Counts of cells are not counts of independent replications.

readings.a: 1 - p_o is the share of the common persons whose per-person verdict depends on which of the two splits is used; it is the number read for the paper. p_e is the agreement expected if the two splits' verdicts were paired independently with their observed marginal distributions (three categories); p_o near p_e says the splits agree on who crosses little more than such a pairing would, and does not prove independence. kappa is written as the standard chance-corrected summary, not as a threshold test and not as the share of persons whose verdict changes.
readings.b: The direction table: a surplus of '1->0' over '0->1' equals (up to the 1/2 cases) the difference of the two shares on the common persons; it is a description of how the splits differ, not of which is right.
readings.c: The agreement of a stage is not read as the reliability of the stage's components (v6l, v6n part 3) and is not compared in size with another stage's as a test; stages differ in number of features and in shares (p_e depends on the shares).
readings.d: Disagreement measures the sensitivity of the whole procedure to the split: the noise of splitting a person's sentences, the difference between what the splits compare (halves: earlier against later writing; odd/even interleaves), each split's own cell scale (from its own rule persons), and the rows' random plan as it falls on each split's parts. v6r does not separate these; it does not count a common-scale variant or random two-part splits (appendix H describes that procedure only).
readings.e: For the paper: if the verdict changes with the split for a sizable share of persons, a per-person report must name the split and should not be read as a property of the person independent of it (recommendation ii-c); v6r says how large that share is on these persons and rows, not in general.
readings.intervals: every interval is over the common persons with the verdicts held fixed (each split's cell scale and v6n's one random plan per person); it is not the uncertainty of rerunning the operations or of choosing other splits, and an interval of [1, 1] when all agree is not a precise population estimate.

checks.reuse: before any new quantity is reported, and stopping the run otherwise: v6n's persons and count persons; per dataset, split and row, v6n's rule cell of every stage (stage, R_loc and R_mean: persons, share and interval; paired difference), recomputed as in v6p's rule_keep, so that each split's contributions give v6n's share; I[2]'s contributions on I's rule persons give v6q's share and interval; v6p's ledger rebuilt per split and row gives v6p's written plan.
checks.construction: the persons are indexed alike in both splits (the same count persons); every contribution is 0, 1/2 or 1 and every distance finite; the 3 x 3 table adds to the common persons; p_o, p_e, the shares and the category proportions are recomputed from the table; the identity of written_plan.table holds (1e-9); I[2]'s common set equals I's.
checks.sets: every written cell's common set is admitted under both splits (written_plan); the whole ledgers are checked again at the end (stop if a new set of 1-4 persons is derivable).
checks.missing: as v6n: a summary over fewer than 5 persons is not written; a non-finite value stops the run.

prediction: Claude's, written before running; exploratory guesses kept apart from the results, not tests. P1: at LWP inside_75 and inside_100, R_loc's p_o is at least 0.75 in both rows. P2: over the primary cells written with kappa defined, 1 - p_o is at least 0.20 in at least half (denominator: those cells; 'not evaluable' if none). P3: I's p_o at LWP inside_75 and inside_100 is below 0.80 in both rows. P4: I[2]'s kappa is below I's at LWP inside_100 (same common persons; 'not evaluable' if either kappa is not written). A prediction with a cell not written is 'not evaluable'. No new value has been seen.
main_cells: fixed before running, shown first: the read-first cells (I, I[2], R_loc at LWP inside_75 and inside_100); then per dataset a table over the stages and primary rows (common persons, rule persons per split and one-split-only, 1 - p_o and p_o's interval, p_e, kappa and interval, the two shares, '1->0', '0->1', the 1/2 cases); then the shuffles; then over the counted primary cells the number of cells written, withheld and fixed, and the distribution of 1 - p_o and kappa (min, median, max), which depends on which cells could be written and is not read as an overall reproducibility index.

record.public: results/prototype_v6r/record.json: counts and summaries over persons and the provenance; no press time, gap, key, text, per-person vector, value, contribution, change or id (ids only as the SHA-256 of their sorted list); a summary over fewer than 5 persons is not written. The data are not redistributed.
record.provenance: git commit and dirty state of the conditions, code and lock; SHA-256 of the conditions, the earlier conditions and records, the code and the data; versions.

limits_written_before: The persons are v6m's with v6m's to v6q's values seen, and the read-first rows were chosen by known gate results: nothing here is a confirmation. Two fixed splits only; a disagreement mixes split noise with the different comparisons the splits make (halves: earlier against later writing) and with the two splits' own cell scales (readings.d). The common persons are a subset of each split's rule persons; their shares are written beside v6n's and are not assumed equal. The stages' common persons may differ, so a comparison between stages mixes the persons. The cells are many and correlated; no correction. The verdict shows sensitivity of a summary to a difference in press times; it says nothing about the cognitive meaning of a pause or the quality of a text.
rerun_rule: as v6k: if a defect of the code is found after the first run, the first record is kept unchanged, the fix and the reason are committed, and the rerun is reported separately beside the first.
generator: as v6k (checked by v6k's code against v6k's conditions).
implementation: the bootstrap interval is v6.ci (2.5th and 97.5th numpy percentiles, linear); the per-person contributions are v6o's contrib_base_change through v6p's rule_keep (checked against v6n's shares) and, for I[2], v6q's with_i2 and contrib (checked against v6q's record).
